horizontal_tail.name: Horizontal tail spar
horizontal_tail.model: Timoshenko beam FEA, 2 DOF/node, 21 sizing stations + Saint-Venant root-warping stress recovery
assumptions: Same solver and stations as the contract FeaResult; optimisation scales t_f and t_w linearly root→tip
Gauges clamped to Raymer minimums t_f ≥ 2.0 mm, t_w ≥ 1.5 mm
Mass is one tail half (multiply by 2)
Tail load case and planform from the tail sizing: Raymer 2ed Eqs. 14.12-14.13, C_n (p. 347), Table 4.3
horizontal_tail.convergence_note: Stations fixed by the spar sizing (21 nodes).

metrics.governing: outer cap fibre at y = 0.00 m

ai_proposal.rationale: The baseline horizontal tail spar has a generous margin of 1.4628 governed by bending in the outer cap fibre at the root (y = 0.00 m). Scaling both root and tip gauges down to the 0.60 minimum limit increases peak stress to roughly 229 MPa, maintaining a safe margin near 0.48 (well above the 0.10 requirement) while achieving maximum possible mass reduction.

ai_proposal.verdict: accepted: solver confirms the constraint and a near-optimal objective

min_mass.rationale: The baseline horizontal tail spar has a generous margin of 1.4628 governed by bending in the outer cap fibre at the root (y = 0.00 m). Scaling both root and tip gauges down to the 0.60 minimum limit increases peak stress to roughly 229 MPa, maintaining a safe margin near 0.48 (well above the 0.10 requirement) while achieving maximum possible mass reduction.

ai_proposal.rationale: Bending and shear loads peak at the root station (137 MPa) and decay rapidly toward the unloaded tip. Shifting structural mass from the lightly loaded tip (k_tip = 0.60) to reinforce the governing root cap and web (k_root = 1.35) substantially increases the minimum safety margin without exceeding the baseline mass.

max_margin.rationale: Every zone is already at minimum gauge (sheet ≥ 0.50 mm): peak σ_vM 137 MPa, margin +1.46. The part is minimum-gauge governed, so no gauge change helps; a lighter design needs thinner stock or a different section, not re-gauging.

ai_proposal.rationale: Peak von Mises stress occurs at the clamped root outer cap fibre due to cantilever bending and Saint-Venant warping. Maximizing root gauge thickness (k_root = 1.45) while tapering the lightly stressed tip to its minimum bound (k_tip = 0.60) maximally reduces root stress within the 1.05x baseline mass budget.
